title: Shortest Palindrome by Prepending
prompt:
Implement `shortest_palindrome_prefix(s)` to form the shortest palindrome obtainable by adding characters only before `s`. You may not append or insert characters elsewhere. Return the resulting string.

Find the longest prefix of `s` that is already a palindrome. If that prefix has length `k`, reverse the remaining suffix `s[k:]` and prepend it to `s`. The input may contain any Python string character, including punctuation such as `#`; do not rely on a literal separator that could collide with input.

Target O(n) time and O(n) space. A KMP/LPS prefix-function pass over `list(s) + [unique_sentinel] + list(reversed(s))` is one deterministic approach. Empty and already-palindromic strings should be returned unchanged.

example.reasoning: The longest palindromic prefix is `'aa'`; reversing the remaining suffix `'b'` gives the only needed prefix.
